entries.title: 9-nine-: Episode 1
entries.subtitle: A different route through the mystery
entries.summary: The first instalment in the series focuses on the first of the four heroines, Miyako Kujo. After finding a petrified human in their college town, Shiromitsugawa City, Kakeru and Miyako work together to investigate the culprit behind this incident.
body: The first instalment in the series focuses on the first of the four heroines, Miyako Kujo. After finding a petrified human in their college town, Shiromitsugawa City, Kakeru and Miyako work together to investigate the culprit behind this incident.

Shiromitsugawa City connects an ordinary student setting to a supernatural mystery. An earthquake breaks a sacred object at Hakuda Tsukumo Shrine, and artifacts from another world give people unusual abilities. Kakeru Niimi investigates a series of petrifications alongside the people drawn into that disturbance.

The visual novel presents the mystery through illustrated scenes, dialogue and a changing point of view. This episode is one dated release within that larger structure. Its Japanese title is Kokonotsu Kokonoka Kokonoiro, and its original Windows release precedes the later English Steam edition and the combined console editions.

entries.title: 9-nine-: Episode 4
entries.subtitle: A different route through the mystery
entries.summary:
The fourth instalment in the series focuses on the final heroine, Noa Yuki, branching off from the third game, Haruiro Harukoi Harunokaze. Having uncovered the mastermind behind the incidents, and realizing Noa's Artifact is the key to defeating the mastermind, Kakeru divulges everything he knows about the matter. Together, they oppose the mastermind and uncover the final secrets behind the Artifacts that arrived in their world.
Due to the story structure of this game, it is strongly recommended that this game be played only after completing the previous three games.

entries.title: 9-nine-: New Episode
entries.subtitle: Returning after the mystery
entries.summary: New Episode returns to the four heroines after the events of the preceding releases. Short after-stories revisit Miyako, Sora, Haruka and Noa, while a further scenario addresses the unfinished task that remains for Kakeru.
body: New Episode returns to the four heroines after the events of the preceding releases. Short after-stories revisit Miyako, Sora, Haruka and Noa, while a further scenario addresses the unfinished task that remains for Kakeru.

The Japanese release is titled Shinsho. Rather than introducing another separate starting route, it acts as an epilogue to the earlier episodes. Familiar characters and unresolved events become material for a conclusion that assumes knowledge of the preceding mysteries.

The after-story format changes the pace of the visual novel. Instead of beginning another investigation with an unfamiliar cast, it returns to people the reader already knows. Smaller scenes and the consequences of earlier events give the series room to consider what remains after its central mystery.

An epilogue across the routes
Time after the ending

entries.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Night Road
entries.subtitle: A place within the World of Darkness
entries.summary: Night Road follows a vampire courier across the Southwestern United States. Delivering the elders' secrets means navigating factions, other vampires and the danger that arrives with daylight. The road connects private decisions to a larger political world.
body: Night Road follows a vampire courier across the Southwestern United States. Delivering the elders' secrets means navigating factions, other vampires and the danger that arrives with daylight. The road connects private decisions to a larger political world.

Marquis stays close to the tabletop game's rules. Character creation and abilities shape the available choices, while the courier premise lets the narrative move between communities rather than remaining inside a single city.

Written by Kyle Marquis and published by Choice of Games, this is a text-based interactive novel. The player creates a character and selects responses that change the direction of the story. Choices and character information carry the action; a conventional moving game world is replaced by a narrative the reader helps shape.
story_headings: A place within the World of Darkness
Perspective shapes the choices
An interactive novel

entries.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Out for Blood
entries.subtitle: A place within the World of Darkness
entries.summary: Out for Blood changes the perspective from vampire to human hunter. A threatened town becomes the setting for gathering allies, investigating the supernatural and deciding how to confront creatures with far more power than an ordinary person.
body: Out for Blood changes the perspective from vampire to human hunter. A threatened town becomes the setting for gathering allies, investigating the supernatural and deciding how to confront creatures with far more power than an ordinary person.

The difference in viewpoint matters: the same World of Darkness setting becomes a place to investigate and survive from outside its ruling supernatural society. Knowledge of opponents and relationships with other people help define the choices available to the player.

Written by Jim Dattilo and published by Choice of Games, this is a text-based interactive novel. The player creates a character and selects responses that change the direction of the story. Choices and character information carry the action; a conventional moving game world is replaced by a narrative the reader helps shape.

entries.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Parliament of Knives
entries.subtitle: A place within the World of Darkness
entries.summary: Parliament of Knives places a vampire inside the unstable politics of Ottawa. The disappearance of the city's Prince creates an opening for competing loyalties, personal ambition and betrayal within an undead hierarchy.
body: Parliament of Knives places a vampire inside the unstable politics of Ottawa. The disappearance of the city's Prince creates an opening for competing loyalties, personal ambition and betrayal within an undead hierarchy.

Dean adapts the tabletop mechanics more loosely than Night Road. Alliances and judgments about other characters give the political setting its structure. The player's decisions become a way to explore how authority survives when everyone around it has a different interest.

Written by Jeffrey Dean and published by Choice of Games, this is a text-based interactive novel. The player creates a character and selects responses that change the direction of the story. Choices and character information carry the action; a conventional moving game world is replaced by a narrative the reader helps shape.

entries.title: Vampire: The Masquerade - Sins of the Sires
entries.subtitle: A place within the World of Darkness
entries.summary: Sins of the Sires follows a vampire in Athens, where an ancient vampire plans to rule over humans as a god. Its Greek setting places personal identity and the pressures of undead society alongside a struggle over power.
body: Sins of the Sires follows a vampire in Athens, where an ancient vampire plans to rule over humans as a god. Its Greek setting places personal identity and the pressures of undead society alongside a struggle over power.

The interactive novel gives its protagonist choices about relationships, allegiance and the self they want to preserve. Its setting offers another viewpoint within the shared World of Darkness rather than continuing the courier, hunter or Ottawa stories directly.
